units.text: Amazon ElastiCache keeps frequently requested data in memory. It can answer repeat reads more quickly and reduce the work your database has to do. Suppose an app needs the product catalog. The first path shows a cache hit. The app checks ElastiCache, finds a usable copy, and returns it without another database read. The second path shows a miss. When the catalog isn't in the cache, the app reads it from the database.

The app saves a copy in ElastiCache so the next request has a chance to hit. This pattern is called cache-aside because the app fills the cache. The database still owns the original. Cached copies can expire, and changes to the original aren't instantly reflected in a saved copy. Decide how much staleness the app can accept.
